Verification and validation protocol

Source: vignettes/validation.Rmd
validation.Rmd

Two different questions

  • Computational verification: does the code implement the published equations correctly? Answered by unit tests (closed forms, numerical integration, independent transcriptions, block equivalence) and by cross-checks against chillR and degday (inst/verification/verify_references.R).
  • Empirical validation: do the estimates agree with indices computed from independent observations? This requires station data and is not answered by any WorldClim experiment.

No claim of predictive superiority of one method over another should be made without empirical validation.

Verification summary

Check Reference Max. abs. difference

Utah model chillR 0.77 0
Chilling hours 0-7.2 chillR 0.77 0
Day length chillR 0.77 < 1e-14
Linvill hourly (night = "chillr") chillR 0.77 < 1e-13
GDD sine/triangle, single/double, horizontal degday 0.4.0 (UC IPM) < 1e-12
pchip_mp, 365 and 366 days tempify 0.1.6 < 1e-13

Protocol for empirical validation with hourly stations

  1. Data. Stations with hourly temperature (e.g. agrometeorological networks such as Agromet INIA or CEAZA in Chile), at least 5 complete years, with documented quality control. Reject days with more than 2 missing hours; fill isolated gaps of 1-2 hours by linear interpolation and report them.
  2. Reference values. Compute “observed” indices directly from hourly data: degree_hours(by_day = TRUE), chill_hours_hourly(), chill_units(), chill_portions(), over the same accumulation periods.
  3. Estimates to evaluate.
    1. daily extremes from the station plus each daily method (analytical GDD and chilling hours; Linvill or sine reconstruction for Utah/Dynamic);
    2. monthly station climatology densified with pchip_mp;
    3. WorldClim cell containing the station. Level (a) isolates the diurnal model error, (b) adds densification error,
    4. adds spatial interpolation error.
  4. Metrics per index, period and station: bias =e‾= \bar{e}, MAE, RMSE, relative error e/Oe / O where OO is not near zero (not for Utah units, which can be zero or negative), and Pearson correlation across years.
  5. Stratification. By season (monthly), by threshold (sensitivity to the base temperature and chilling interval), and by geographic setting (coast, valley, foothills).
  6. Spatial evaluation. Leave-one-station-out comparison of level (c); map residuals against elevation and distance to the coast.
  7. Reporting. Report sample sizes, gaps filled, the exact package versions (sessionInfo(), tempify_version()), and uncertainty intervals (bootstrap across years).
metrics <- function(est, obs) {
  e <- est - obs
  c(bias = mean(e), mae = mean(abs(e)), rmse = sqrt(mean(e^2)),
    r = stats::cor(est, obs))
}
